subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` land with existing archive-retention deletion/reporting for stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` transcript archives, or should this wait for the broader archive-preservation policy decision?
rationale: The patch is technically coherent and proven, but it makes a user-visible cleanup command more explicitly delete archived session artifacts, which overlaps the data-preservation concern in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56609.

options.title: Land Current Retention Behavior
options.body: Accept that the existing retention rules own stale deleted/reset archive cleanup, with dry-run/apply reporting making the deletion visible to operators.

options.title: Pause For Retention Policy
options.body: Hold this PR until maintainers decide whether `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archives should remain removable or move to a preservation-oriented archive model.

options.title: Narrow To Reporting Only
options.body: Ask for a revised patch that reports only cleanup already triggered by another lifecycle action and does not force a standalone archive-retention scan.

recommendation.title: Land Current Retention Behavior
recommendation.body: Accept that the existing retention rules own stale deleted/reset archive cleanup, with dry-run/apply reporting making the deletion visible to operators.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently changed forced session cleanup and disk-budget ordering in the same decision surface, making them the best routing candidate for the merge-risk choice.
